basic_info.name: MEDCOD and Note2Chat
basic_info.description: Two research prototypes, five years apart, that together define the history-taking dialogue pattern Module C depends on. MEDCOD (Curai Health, ML4H 2021) is the archetype of a hybrid dialogue system in which a deterministic, expert-system dialogue manager owns the history-taking state and decides what to ask next, while a neural generator only decides how to phrase it: its dialogue manager pairs a conversation tracker and a QMR-lineage medical knowledge base (830 diseases, 2,052 findings) with a 'Next Finding' expert system that selects the next target finding in an explainable, auditable way, and a separate DialoGPT-Medium NLG module controlled by two codes (target finding + emote) produces the natural-language question. Its load-bearing fact is that the structured slot state - which finding is being asked, and which findings are present/absent - is a first-class, machine-readable object independent of the surface wording. Note2Chat (A*STAR/NTU/NUS/SGH, AAAI 2026) is the modern, note-driven counterpart: it trains a Qwen2.5-7B doctor agent by converting real MIMIC-IV discharge notes into 8,944 synthetic doctor-patient dialogues, then applies a three-stage fine-tuning pipeline (SFT + self-augmented trajectory sampling + DPO) and a single-turn reasoning paradigm in which every turn is treated as one Markov decision step with a hidden Summary+Planning reasoning block. Note2Chat reports the largest measured jump in multi-turn history taking to date, +16.9 F1 and +21.0 Top-1 diagnostic accuracy over GPT-4o. Neither emits a standards-conformant clinical document; MEDCOD's contribution is the deterministic-state architecture, Note2Chat's is the scalable training and per-turn reward-supervision recipe.
basic_info.organization: MEDCOD - Curai Health (Curai, Inc.), with academic co-authors from NYU and Drexel; Note2Chat - Institute of High Performance Computing (IHPC), A*STAR, with Nanyang Technological University, National University of Singapore and Singapore General Hospital
basic_info.country: MEDCOD - United States (Palo Alto / San Francisco, California); Note2Chat - Singapore
basic_info.status: research. Both are research prototypes with released code; MEDCOD's repository has been dormant since December 2024 and its paper dates from 2021, while Note2Chat was published at AAAI 2026 with its repository active into March 2026.

technical_features.what_it_does: MEDCOD performs automated medical history taking in dialogue. Its dialogue manager maintains the authoritative clinical state: a conversation tracker records demographics, reason for encounter, findings reported, and the text of prior questions and answers; a Next Finding expert system consumes patient demographics plus reported findings and, using a QMR-style knowledge base (diseases, findings, evoking strength and term frequency, plus human-written patient-answerable questions for every finding), computes the differential and selects the single next patient-reportable finding to ask about. An emotion classifier predicts an 'emote' control code (Affirmative, Empathy, Apology, None) from the conversation context. A fine-tuned DialoGPT-Medium NLG module then renders the target finding as varied, human-like, appropriately empathetic natural language. The separation is the point: the expert system decides what to ask in an explainable, auditable way, and the neural module only decides how to ask. Note2Chat solves the same information-gathering problem with a learned policy instead of an expert system: it frames history taking as a partially observable sequential decision process, trains a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct doctor agent on note-derived dialogues, and at each turn emits a hidden reasoning block (a running Summary of the conversation plus a Planning rationale for the next action) before either asking a follow-up question or issuing a ranked differential diagnosis. For Module C the load-bearing distinction is that MEDCOD's output includes an explicit structured finding/slot state that a deterministic renderer can consume, whereas Note2Chat's clinically meaningful state lives in free-text reasoning blocks and a final ranked diagnosis list, and it actively diagnoses.
technical_features.architecture: MEDCOD - deliberately hybrid modular + deep learning. Dialogue manager = (1) conversation tracker (state), (2) Next Finding expert system over a medical KB of 830 diseases and 2,052 findings with evoking-strength / term-frequency relations and per-finding patient-answerable questions, (3) emotion classifier built from Sentence-BERT (paraphrase-mpnet-base-v2) embeddings of three context pieces (previous question, patient response, target finding), PCA to 70 components, and logistic regression over 4 emote classes. NLG = DialoGPT-Medium fine-tuned on 143,600 conversational instances (batch 16 x 16 grad-accum, 3 epochs, lr 1e-4, Adam) with control codes prepended at training and inference. Data was bootstrapped with a Structured Clinical Case Simulator over the KB and with GPT-3 (temperature 0.65) for question paraphrasing. Note2Chat - a training-and-inference framework rather than a fixed architecture. Doctor agent = Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct fine-tuned with LoRA (rank 8, alpha 32, dropout 0.05). Three-stage pipeline: SFT on note-guided dialogues (3 epochs, batch 128, lr 5e-5, cosine, warmup 0.1), then self-augmented trajectory sampling (doctor does self-play against a Qwen2.5-32B simulated patient, rollouts filtered for correct diagnosis and highest finding recall), then DPO (2 epochs, lr 1e-5) on top/bottom reward-scored dialogues. A second variant adds single-turn reasoning: each turn is decomposed into an independent MDP decision with a hidden <think> block (Summary + Planning), a turn-level process reward, and turn-level DPO. All training on a server with 8 x NVIDIA H200 GPUs; patient simulator and automatic evaluator are both Qwen2.5-32B.
technical_features.inputs: MEDCOD - patient age and sex, reason for encounter / chief complaint, the sequence of prior questions and patient responses, and the set of findings already asserted present or absent; internally the KB supplies finding-disease relations. Text only, no audio, no documents. Note2Chat - at inference, a chief complaint plus accumulated dialogue turns from a simulated or real patient. At training, MIMIC-IV discharge notes (specifically the History of Present Illness section and the primary diagnosis) for 4,972 patients across 10 conditions (Asthma, COPD, Cellulitis, Chronic venous insufficiency, Deep vein thrombosis, Erysipelas, Heart Failure, Necrotising Fasciitis, Pneumonia, Trauma/hematoma). No vitals, imaging, labs or structured FHIR input.
technical_features.outputs: MEDCOD - a natural-language follow-up question for the current turn, plus the internal structured state (next finding target, emote control code, findings asserted present/absent, and the KB's differential distribution). It does not generate a clinical note, summary or coded document; the paper's contribution is the question-generation and dialogue-management layer, and the structured state is the artifact a downstream renderer would need. Note2Chat - a sequence of follow-up questions, per-turn hidden Summary and Planning blocks (interpretability artifacts), and a final ranked list of K candidate diagnoses (K=5 in training, top-1/2/3 reported). It explicitly produces a differential diagnosis and does not produce a coded clinical document.
technical_features.standards_compliance: [uncertain] Neither system conforms to any clinical document or terminology standard, and neither claims to. MEDCOD's knowledge base is a bespoke internal expert system; the paper makes no mention of SNOMED CT, LOINC, ICD, HL7 or FHIR, and the finding/disease identities are internal codes. Note2Chat uses ICD-10 codes only as a selection filter to pick which MIMIC-IV notes to include; there is no output coding, no terminology binding and no FHIR resource or Composition. Both are evaluated on question quality and diagnostic accuracy, not on document conformance. Any Module C mapping from either system's state or outputs to NRCeS OPConsultRecord sections would have to be built entirely by MediKiosk.
technical_features.offline_capability: [uncertain] Not addressed by either paper, and neither is designed around offline operation. MEDCOD's components are small enough in principle to run locally (DialoGPT-Medium and MPNet-base SBERT plus a logistic-regression classifier and a static KB), so a descendent could plausibly run on-device, but no local storage, encryption, store-and-forward or sync mechanism is described and MEDCOD's own dependency on GPT-3 was training-time only. Note2Chat reports no offline story; its doctor agent is a 7B-parameter model, which does not fit a ~4GB CPU/iGPU kiosk budget, and training required 8 x H200 GPUs, so it is inherently a server-class or cloud workload.
technical_features.languages_supported: English only, for both. MEDCOD's data comes from a US telehealth platform and its KB questions are English; the paper explicitly lists speech recognition/synthesis and non-English capability as future work, not present functionality. Note2Chat's supervision source is English MIMIC-IV discharge notes and its prompts, metrics and evaluators are English. Neither reports Hindi, Devanagari, Hinglish or any Indic-language capability.
technical_features.deployment_model: MEDCOD - research prototype; never described as deployed. Curai commercialised a separate text-first virtual primary-care service, but MEDCOD the artifact is a research pipeline with reference code, not a shipped product. Note2Chat - research prototype; inference requires a fine-tuned 7B model (server or GPU-class hardware) and the paper's experiments ran on 8 x NVIDIA H200, with a Qwen2.5-32B patient simulator and a Qwen2.5-32B evaluator. No clinic-LAN, kiosk, room-server or edge deployment is described for either.

performance_metrics.accuracy_or_quality_metrics: MEDCOD: (1) End-to-end preference, 30 common chief complaints, five medical professionals role-playing patient and doctor simultaneously against both systems, three labels per case: MEDCOD scored 63 out of a possible 90 vs the template 'Expert' baseline, i.e. preferred in over half of conversations; on mutually exclusive picks, 54.4% MEDCOD vs 17.8% Expert (27.8% equal), and with majority voting across complaints 66.7% MEDCOD vs 6.6% Expert. (2) NLG module rated by five medical professionals on 100 instances on a 1-5 scale: Medical Accuracy 4.872, Fluency 4.730, Empathy 3.892, versus Expert 4.956 / 4.942 / 2.772 and MEDCOD-no-Emote 4.882 / 4.832 / 2.806 - paraphrase diversity and empathy were added without materially degrading medical consistency or fluency, and the empathy gain was significant. (3) Emotion classifier on a human-augmented test set: 0.9 accuracy, macro-F1 0.8, PR-AUC 0.69, with precision >= recall on the non-None classes by design. (4) GPT-3-generated question paraphrases passed medical-consistency validation for 78% of finding-question pairs. Note2Chat: main results on the MIMIC-IV-derived test set, Note2Chat-ST (single-turn) F1 46.1, Recall 46.2, Precision 54.5, Top-1 70.0, Top-2 81.2, Top-3 84.4 at 17.3 turns on average; Note2Chat-MT F1 43.8, Recall 55.4, Top-1 62.0 at 27.5 turns. Baselines: GPT-4o F1 29.2, Top-1 49.0; Gemini-2.5-flash F1 26.6, Top-1 51.4; MedGemma-27B F1 27.9, Top-1 52.8; DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B F1 29.6, Top-1 37.2; base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct F1 19.6, Top-1 38.8. Gains over GPT-4o: +16.9 F1 and +21.0 Top-1 (relative +57.53% information gathering and +42.86% diagnosis). Ablation for single-turn: base 37.5 average -> SFT 50.6 -> +self-augmentation 56.8 -> +DPO 63.7 average. Clinician comparison on a small held-out set of 20 cases across 10 diseases showed comparable diagnostic accuracy and information gathering.
performance_metrics.latency: [uncertain] Neither paper reports latency or throughput. MEDCOD gives no wall-clock numbers for question generation despite describing latency constraints as a design concern; its local NLG model is small (DialoGPT-Medium). Note2Chat gives no inference latency, but its single-turn variant completes dialogues in fewer turns (17.3) than its multi-turn variant (27.5), GPT-4o (22.9), o4-mini (27.0) or Gemini-2.5-flash (31.9), which is the paper's efficiency proxy rather than a timing measurement.
performance_metrics.resource_requirements: MEDCOD: DialoGPT-Medium (a ~345M-parameter class model) plus paraphrase-mpnet-base-v2 SBERT embeddings plus a logistic-regression classifier plus a static knowledge base; training was modest (143,600 instances, effective batch 64, 3 epochs) and would fit a single mid-range GPU, while inference is CPU-plausible though no RAM/VRAM footprint is published. Note2Chat: base model Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (7B parameters), trained with LoRA on a server with 8 NVIDIA H200 GPUs, plus a Qwen2.5-32B patient simulator and a Qwen2.5-32B evaluator; no inference RAM/VRAM figure is published, but a 7B model is far outside a ~4GB CPU/iGPU kiosk budget.
performance_metrics.scale_metrics: MEDCOD: dataset built from a KB of 830 diseases and 2,052 findings; 3,600 doctor-edited question instances; 500 most frequent findings paraphrased; 143,600 training conversation instances; evaluation on 30 chief complaints and 100 NLG instances with five medical professionals. Reference code in the Curai research repository, which has no license file and has been dormant since December 2024. Note2Chat: 4,972 patients, 10 conditions, 8,944 synthetic dialogues averaging 17.8 turns, 67,077 successful self-play rollouts, 11,403 dialogue-level preference pairs, 4,472 training and 500 test patients, 80,537 context-aware single-turn interactions and 95,811 turn-level preference pairs; GitHub repository (zhentingsheng/Note2Chat) created 2025-11-11, last push 2026-03-24, 5 stars, 0 forks, 1 open issue.
performance_metrics.evaluation_protocol: MEDCOD (peer-reviewed, ML4H 2021, PMLR v158): four evaluations. End-to-end A/B preference with five medical professionals role-playing both roles against a template baseline over 30 chief complaints (three labels per case, majority voting); NLG multi-axis rating (medical consistency, fluency, empathy) on 100 context instances by five medical professionals; emotion-classifier evaluation against a human-augmented test set with majority voting; and human validation of GPT-3 paraphrase correctness. Sample sizes are small and the raters are in-house medical professionals, not independent blinded reviewers. Note2Chat (peer-reviewed, AAAI 2026): offline evaluation on a held-out MIMIC-IV subset using a Qwen2.5-32B simulated patient (itself assessed for information control 82.66 and factual conflict 0.29 for the 32B variant) and a Qwen2.5-32B automatic evaluator that checks how many ground-truth note findings were elicited and where the true diagnosis ranked. Metrics are precision, recall, F1 and Top-K diagnostic accuracy. Robustness is shown via a component ablation, recall broken down by the SOCRATES axes (Site, Onset, Character, Radiation, Associated symptoms, Timing, Exacerbating/relieving factors, Severity, plus History) - where even GPT-4o scored only 13.6% on Site and 10.1% on Severity - and a limited comparison with one practising clinician on 20 cases, which the authors describe as far from conclusive. Both are peer-reviewed at their venues; neither has been independently replicated, and Note2Chat's findings are tied to 10 conditions from one source dataset.

milestone_significance.relevance_to_module_c: MEDCOD is the architectural precedent for Module C's central design bet: keep the history-taking state in a deterministic, inspectable component and let a neural model handle only surface language. Its Next Finding expert system is precisely the kind of rationale-traceable slot selector that a deterministic summary renderer needs, because the system already knows which finding is being asked and which findings are present or absent - so a renderer can emit those slots with per-field provenance instead of parsing free text. Its second-hand relevance is that it demonstrates the hybrid modularise-the-what / learn-the-how split that MediKiosk cites for a CPU-budget kiosk, and its use of a controlled vocabulary of findings (830 diseases, 2,052 findings queried with structured attributes) is conceptually the same move as mapping elicited history into a fixed SOCRATES/Dashavidha ontology before rendering. Note2Chat is the opposite lesson: it shows that an end-to-end fine-tuned LLM can dramatically beat proprietary baselines at multi-turn elicitation (F1 46.1 and Top-1 70.0 vs GPT-4o's 29.2 and 49.0) and that decomposing a dialogue into single-turn MDP decisions with hidden Summary+Planning blocks yields interpretable per-turn supervision - directly relevant to how a summariser should consume a turn-by-turn bundle and how confidence/coverage might be scored. But Note2Chat also diagnoses (ranked differentials), trains on MIMIC-IV (US data), needs a 7B model and H200 GPUs, and is written in English, so it validates the elicitation-state and per-turn-provenance ideas while warning against the LLM-centric, diagnosis-emitting, server-heavy path.
milestone_significance.what_to_adopt_or_reject: Adopt from MEDCOD: (a) the strict separation of a deterministic state/decision layer from an LLM phrasing layer - for Module C this means the SOAP/OPConsultRecord renderer should be a deterministic template engine that reads frozen HistoryBundle slots, never an LLM asked to re-derive meaning; (b) an explicit per-turn finding/slot state (which finding, present/absent, confidence) as the machine-readable contract between dialogue and renderer, which is exactly the provenance substrate MediKiosk wants; (c) the controlled finding vocabulary and per-finding patient-answerable questions as a model for a bilingual SOCRATES/Dashavidha question bank; (d) emotion/intent tagging as a cheap, auditable way to keep the kiosk conversation humane without a large dialogue model. Reject from MEDCOD: GPT-3-based synthetic data bootstrapping and any cloud dependency, and the assumption that a 2,000-finding KB needs to be maintained in-house. Adopt from Note2Chat: (a) using routinely available notes as silver supervision instead of scarce dialogue data - directly transferable to building a synthetic history-to-summary dataset without patient dialogue corpora; (b) the hidden Summary + Planning reasoning block as an interpretability and per-field-provenance device inside the summary pipeline; (c) the recall/SOCRATES-axis breakdown as the right way to measure whether a summary is missing Site/Onset/Severity-type details, and its demonstration that off-the-shelf models are weakest exactly there; (d) turn-efficiency measurement (questions asked to reach completeness) as a kiosk KPI. Reject from Note2Chat: emitting a differential diagnosis or any management suggestion, since MediKiosk is elicit-never-diagnose and Note2Chat's whole reward optimises toward diagnosis; the 7B-model and H200-GPU resource envelope, which is incompatible with the ~4GB CPU/iGPU kiosk; reliance on MIMIC-IV (US, restricted) for any India deployment; and single-source evaluation on only 10 conditions.
milestone_significance.limitations_and_risks: MEDCOD is old (2021) and narrow: it solves question generation, not summarisation or document emission, and it does not produce a clinical note at all. Its evidence base is small (30 chief complaints, 100 NLG instances, five in-house medical professionals) with no independent or blinded evaluation, and its end-to-end result is a preference comparison against a template baseline rather than a clinical-accuracy measurement. Its knowledge base and the GPT-3 paraphrase step are US telehealth artefacts with unknown licensing, and the reference repository has no LICENSE file and has been dormant since December 2024, so the code is legally hazardous to reuse and not maintained. It also never addressed speech, non-English input, offline operation or any standardised output; emotion classification was validated on a small in-house set. Note2Chat is recent but its evidence has structural caveats: it is evaluated on a MIMIC-IV subset restricted to 10 conditions chosen for diagnostic overlap, with a simulated patient and an LLM evaluator sharing the same base model family as the training loop, which risks evaluator-simulator circularity; the clinician comparison is only 20 cases with a single clinician and the authors themselves call it far from conclusive. Its headline gains are diagnostic-accuracy and finding-recall gains, not summary-fidelity gains, and the reward explicitly rewards diagnosis, so its behaviour is antithetical to elicit-never-diagnose. It needs 7B-class inference and H200-class training, uses US-derived restricted data, is English-only, has no offline or FHIR story, and its repository is very early (5 stars, 0 forks, 1 open issue, last push March 2026). Its single-turn decompositions are also generated with a 32B model, so the pipeline's data cost is not trivial.
milestone_significance.differentiator_vs_medikiosk: Neither system competes with MediKiosk's stated differentiation and both leave all five MediKiosk axes open. MEDCOD is a US, English, text-only question generator with no summary, no FHIR/NRCeS emission, no ABDM integration, no offline or India-residency story, no Indic languages, and an unlicensed dormant repository; it differs from MediKiosk by stopping at the dialogue-management layer instead of producing a physician-ready document, but it strengthens MediKiosk's design case by validating the deterministic-state-plus-LLM-phrasing split MediKiosk relies on for CPU-only, auditable operation. Note2Chat is a Singapore/English, GPU-class, diagnosis-producing framework trained on US MIMIC-IV data; it differs sharply from MediKiosk's strict elicit-never-diagnose posture because its objective and reward optimise diagnostic accuracy, and its resource envelope is the opposite of a 4GB CPU/iGPU kiosk, but it strengthens MediKiosk by demonstrating that cheap note-derived supervision can massively improve elicitation completeness and by supplying a recall-by-SOCRATES-axis evaluation that Module C can reuse to prove it captures Site/Onset/Severity detail. In short, both mainly supply architectural and evaluation lessons; they erode none of the offline, India-residency, NRCeS-conformant-emission, per-field-provenance or physician-attestation differentiators.

business_info.license: MEDCOD - no license. The Curai research repository and its MEDCOD subfolder contain no LICENSE file and GitHub reports no detected license, so by default all rights are reserved and the code is not legally reusable for Module C without permission. Note2Chat - MIT License, confirmed from the repository's detected license metadata, and the code is publicly available at github.com/zhentingsheng/Note2Chat.
business_info.pricing: Not applicable to either. Both are free academic research artifacts with no published pricing, no commercial terms and no paid tier; the underlying components are open (DialoGPT, Sentence-BERT, Qwen2.5) but no commercial offering is attached to MEDCOD or Note2Chat themselves.
business_info.funding: MEDCOD - industry-funded research by Curai Health, which as a company has raised roughly USD 38.2M (LinkedIn profile: USD 10.7M Series A, 2018-05-30, and USD 27.5M Series B, 2020-12-16) up to a reported USD 57M across two rounds (Tracxn), with investors including Khosla Ventures, General Catalyst and Morningside; the company was founded in 2017 by Neal Khosla and reports ~101 employees. Note2Chat - public research funding: Singapore's National Research Foundation under the AI Singapore Programme (AISG Award No. AISG2-TC-2023-013) and the SingHealth Duke-NUS Academic Medical Centre / A*STAR Healthcare Translation Partnership grants I24D1AG022 and I24D1AG085.
business_info.commercial_status: Both are unpaid research projects, not products or services. MEDCOD was produced inside a venture-backed company (Curai Health) whose commercial offering is a separate text-first virtual primary-care service; Note2Chat is publicly funded academic work with no commercial offering or government programme attached.

competition_ecosystem.competitors: For the history-taking dialogue layer specifically: Google DeepMind's AMIE and g-AMIE, DoctorAgent-RL, AgentClinic and similar multi-agent clinical dialogue frameworks, MedGemma and BioMistral/HuatuoGPT-o1 domain models, and the commercial ambient/patient-intake systems (Abridge, Nuance DAX Copilot, Ambience, Sunoh.ai, Eka Care/EkaScribe, Clearstep AI Clinical Intake, Phreesia, MiiHealth AI). MEDCOD's 2021-era peers were end-to-end neural dialogue systems; Note2Chat's own related-work section names AMIE, DoctorAgent-RL and RL-based diagnosis systems as the closest alternatives. No competitor combines offline operation, ABDM/NRCeS emission and patient-kiosk elicitation.
competition_ecosystem.integrations: None for either system. MEDCOD's purpose-built knowledge base is internal to Curai and the reference repository is standalone; no EHR, HIS, ABDM HIP/HIU/PHR, health-locker or messaging integration exists. Note2Chat is trained and evaluated entirely offline on MIMIC-IV and ships as training/inference scripts with no clinical system integration, no FHIR endpoint and no ABDM role. Neither provides anything Module C could directly wire into an ABDM gateway.
competition_ecosystem.ecosystem_notes: The surrounding ecosystem is moving toward both ends these two papers bracket: Google's AMIE program has moved into real-world clinical feasibility studies and expert-level video consultations, while academic work increasingly trains open small models (Qwen, MedGemma) on note-derived supervision the way Note2Chat does. This is a tailwind for MediKiosk's architectural instincts - deterministic state ownership plus a small, replaceable language layer - and for its evaluation plan, since the note-derived silver-supervision recipe and the SOCRATES-axis recall breakdown are both cheap to replicate on Indian data. The counter-pressure is that the visible competition (Google, funded US/Indian ambient scribes) is cloud-first, English-first and diagnosis-capable, so judges may compare MediKiosk against systems far outside the kiosk's hardware and regulatory envelope; MediKiosk should therefore lean on the offline, ABDM-conformance and elicit-never-diagnose axes, which none of these research systems address at all.

history.release_date: MEDCOD - first released as arXiv preprint 2111.09381 on 2021-11-17 and published in the Proceedings of Machine Learning for Health (ML4H) 2021, PMLR volume 158, pages 110-129, on 2021-11-28 (presented December 2021). Note2Chat - first released as arXiv preprint 2601.21551 on 2026-01-29 and published at AAAI 2026, with the proceedings version dated 2026-03-14; the GitHub repository was created 2025-11-11.
history.key_milestones: 2017: Curai Health founded by Neal Khosla. 2018-05-30: Curai USD 10.7M Series A. 2020-12-16: Curai USD 27.5M Series B. 2021-11-17/28: MEDCOD released and published at ML4H 2021. 2021-12: Curai research repository hosts the MEDCOD code alongside other projects (CONSCENDI, DERA, MEDOMIT, OSLAT, medical-summarization-ML4H-2021, a dialogue-contextualized re-ranking line). 2023: Curai publishes 'Dialog-Contextualized Re-ranking for Medical History Taking' (Zhu, Valmianski, Kannan, ML4H 2023), continuing the history-taking line. 2024-12-19: last recorded push to the Curai research repository (MEDCOD thereafter dormant). 2025-11-11: Note2Chat GitHub repository created. 2026-01-29: Note2Chat arXiv preprint. 2026-03-14: Note2Chat published at AAAI 2026 (Vol. 40, No. 41, pp. 35149-35157). 2026-03-24: last recorded push to the Note2Chat repository.
history.recent_changes_last_6_months: Inside the six-month window: Note2Chat was published at AAAI 2026 and its repository remained active through 2026-03-24; no further Note2Chat release, model checkpoint or dataset update was found after March 2026. MEDCOD had no activity at all in the window - the paper is from 2021 and its repository has not changed since December 2024, so from a currency standpoint MEDCOD is prior art to be cited for architecture, not a live project to track. The relevant currency movement is in the neighbouring ecosystem rather than in these two artifacts: Google DeepMind's AMIE line published a Nature paper on longitudinal disease management (June 2026) and demonstrated expert-level real-time video consultations (August 2026), and its real-world pre-visit history-taking feasibility study at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center appeared in 2026, all of which raise the benchmark against which a history-taking prototype is judged while still leaving the offline/ABDM/Indic gap open.

market_positioning.target_users: MEDCOD - Curai researchers and clinicians building automated history taking for text-first telehealth; secondarily the academic NLP-for-health community. Note2Chat - academic and industrial researchers working on clinical dialogue, medical LLM training and diagnostic reasoning; secondarily clinicians interested in AI-assisted history taking. Neither targets patients, hospitals or governments directly, and neither is packaged for procurement.
market_positioning.market_segment: Clinical history-taking dialogue systems / medical dialogue research: MEDCOD in the pre-visit intake and symptom-checker tradition, Note2Chat in the LLM clinical-reasoning benchmark and training-framework segment. Adjacent to, but distinct from, ambient clinical scribing, PHR and FHIR tooling.
market_positioning.positioning_statement: MEDCOD positions itself, in its own words, as the first medically consistent and controllable history-taking dialogue system with human-like natural-language expression, whose key idea is to 'integrate the advantage of a traditional modular approach to incorporate (medical) domain knowledge with modern deep learning techniques' - deciding what to ask explainably with an expert system and how to ask humanely with a neural generator. Note2Chat positions itself as 'a generalizable LLM training framework for clinically grounded, proactive history taking' that 'leverages medical notes as a natural and scalable supervision source', shifting 'the focus from diagnosis to high-quality information gathering, better aligning with the exploratory nature of real-world clinical reasoning', and reports state-of-the-art findings-elicitation and diagnostic results with relative gains of +57.53% and +42.86% over GPT-4o.
